story.title: DR Congo Faces Rapid Resurgence of Ebola Epidemic
story.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is grappling with a significant resurgence of Ebola, having recorded nearly 4,000 confirmed cases and over 1,800 deaths. This outbreak, attributed to the Bundibugyo virus, is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history and the fastest-spreading in the country's records.

timeline_highlights.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 1,000 confirmed deaths, according to official government data. The World Health Organization has indicated that the actual number of cases may be significantly higher, potentially two to four times the reported figures.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Becomes Worst in History
timeline_highlights.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the deadliest in the country's history, claiming 1,587 lives and surpassing 3,500 reported cases. This outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, is now recognized as the world's second-largest ever, with no approved vaccine or treatment available.

timeline_highlights.title: New Ebola Treatment Center Opens in Bunia, DR Congo Amid Outbreak
timeline_highlights.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is set to open its largest Ebola treatment center in Bunia this week. This development comes as the World Health Organization reports an intensifying outbreak, with 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths as of July 30. Health authorities aim to enhance response efforts and patient care with the expanded treatment capacity.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Workers in DR Congo Threaten Strikes Over Unpaid Salaries Amid Outbreak
timeline_highlights.summary: Frontline health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly in Ituri province, are threatening to strike due to unpaid salaries while battling a significant Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization has noted that the outbreak is advancing faster than the response efforts, raising concerns about healthcare access and the potential for staff shortages to hinder containment efforts.
key_facts: Frontline health workers in DR Congo are at risk of quitting due to unpaid salaries.

related_stories.title: Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Fauci in contempt
related_stories.summary: The Senate Homeland Security Committee has voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress due to his refusal to answer questions during a recent hearing. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment over 100 times while addressing inquiries related to his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. This contempt finding may lead to further investigations regarding the validity of his constitutional rights against self-incrimination.
